caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response:
The plot illustrates the coverage metric as a function of the number of completions (k), comparing four model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k)”, spans from 2⁰ to 2⁸ on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at integer powers of two (1, 2, 4, ..., 256). The y-axis, labeled “Coverage”, ranges from 0.2 to 1.0 on a linear scale, with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. Four distinct lines are plotted: Llama-3B (solid blue line with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.42 at k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.92 at k=256; Llama-3B + FT (dashed green line with triangular markers) closely tracks Llama-3B, beginning near 0.42 and ending near 0.92, showing near-identical performance; Llama-1B (solid light blue line with circular markers) begins at approximately 0.22 and increases to about 0.72 by k=128, with negligible further growth through k=256; Llama-1B + FT (dashed light green line with triangular markers) starts near 0.27 and reaches approximately 0.77 at k=128, maintaining a consistent ~0.05 higher coverage than its non-fine-tuned counterpart across all k values. All lines exhibit monotonically increasing trends with no dips or plateaus before k=128 for the 1B models.
